name: Data
oneLiner: The text, code, images and feedback that models learn from, and how it's collected, cleaned and licensed.

analogy.text: Ingredients in a recipe: the best chef can't fix spoiled ingredients.
analogy.breaks: Ingredients get used up; data doesn't, but reusing the same data again and again gives diminishing returns, and this 'ingredient' can carry hidden bias, private details or copyright obligations.

examples: Web crawls such as Common Crawl
Curated open datasets such as FineWeb
givesAbove: Training corpora and feedback data that shape what a model can do.
needsBelow: Storage and compute from Cloud & Infrastructure to collect, filter and deduplicate at scale.

walkthrough.title: A recipe page is crawled
walkthrough.text: A blog post on boiling eggs is scooped up in a web crawl, along with thousands of copies of it on scraper sites.

walkthrough.title: Is it allowed?
walkthrough.text: Before it's used, someone should check the blog's licence and whether its robots.txt opted out of AI crawlers. If it did, the page is dropped.

walkthrough.title: Copies out, quality checked, mix set
walkthrough.text: Curation keeps one copy, scores the page as useful, and decides how much cooking text sits beside code, maths and books.

walkthrough.title: Practice questions are generated
walkthrough.text: A model writes new questions and answers about cooking times; curation screens out the ones that are wrong before they reach post-training.

walkthrough.title: People pick the better answer
walkthrough.text: A rater sees two answers to “How long do I boil an egg?” and picks the clearer one. That choice teaches post-training what people prefer.
